To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found a developmental pattern of protein expression for various membrane transporters in human fetuses and newborn liver.

we quantified absolute expression levels of 14 hepatic membrane transporters in 62 human fetal and pediatric liver samples and that protein levels of several of these transporters are developmentally regulated.

we quantified the expression levels of a panel of 13 membrane transporters in a unique cohort of 62 human livers from fetuses and newborn children, and found that transporter protein expression is highly variable and dependent on postmenstrual and gestational age, and not on genetic variation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the developmental regulation of the expression of hepatic membrane transporters in the fetus and newborn.
the identification and characterization of the human fetal and newborn hepatic membrane transporters.
the development of the human liver and the role of membrane transporters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are age‐related differences in the expression of membrane transporters in fetal, newborn, and pediatric livers, and that these differences are not related to mRNA expression.
there is a relationship between postmenstrual and protein expression of various membrane transporters in the human fetal and neonatal liver.

transporter ontogeny is not only a function of gestational age, but also postnatal age.
